_note: BCPSS Instructional Framework (UIFR) Level 4 evidence scaffolds for the curriculum top1 layer. Teacher Mode only. This does NOT guarantee a rating — it makes Level 4 evidence visible and easy to collect. Components mirror the UIFR domains: Prepare, Teach, Reflect & Adjust.
disclaimer: This planning layer helps you make Highly Effective (4) evidence visible and collectable. The actual rating depends on live classroom evidence and observer judgment.

components.title: Prepare 1 — Know your students and self
components.prompt: Name the prior skill and the language/SPED needs this lesson must reach. Plan one scaffold per need that still leads to grade-level mastery.

components.title: Prepare 2 — Use curricular and other resources to prepare
components.prompt: Identify the standard, the aligned task, and the resources (lesson, notes, slides, assessment) you will use to teach it.

components.title: Teach 1 — Facilitate clear, standards-based content learning
components.prompt: State the standard and 'I can' objective so students can name what they are learning and why it matters.

components.title: Teach 2 — Engage students in rigorous work
components.prompt: Provide a grade-level task plus a higher-level prompt and a transfer task; let students show thinking in more than one way.

components.title: Teach 3 — Use intentional questioning
components.prompt: Plan an access, strategy, misconception, justify, and transfer question, and invite a student-generated question.

components.title: Teach 4 — Monitor progress and provide feedback
components.prompt: Check understanding at the beginning, middle, and end; give feedback stems and a revision chance.

components.title: Teach 5 — Facilitate academic talk
components.prompt: Set partner roles and evidence stems so students agree, disagree, add on, and ask for evidence using academic vocabulary.

components.title: Teach 6 — Organize learning-focused routines
components.prompt: Use the Start → Learn → Try → Explain → Check → Reflect flow with materials, timing, transitions, and an early-finisher option.

components.title: Teach 7 — Cultivate a supportive community
components.prompt: Provide a low-risk entry point, an encouragement stem, and language that normalizes productive struggle and revision.

components.title: Reflect & Adjust 1 — Reflect on teaching practice
components.prompt: After the lesson, note what worked, what misconception appeared, and what student work is your evidence.

components.title: Reflect & Adjust 2 — Reflect on data to adjust plans
components.prompt: Use the check data to decide who needs reteach, core practice, language support, or extension next.

questioningLadder.q: What do you already know that can help you start this problem?
Which strategy or model did you choose, and why does it fit?
A student got a different answer doing ___ — where could that go wrong?
What is your evidence that your answer is correct?
Where else could you use this idea, or how would it change if the numbers were different?
What is a question you still have, or one you could ask a classmate?

academicTalkStems: Another way to solve it is ___.

formativeCheckpoints.move: Quick prior-skill check (thumbs / one problem) to see who is ready.
Stop and Jot or partner check on the core skill; scan for the common error.
Exit ticket on the objective; sort responses into reteach / practice / extend.

feedbackStems: Your model shows ___. Add ___ so it matches your equation.
You solved it correctly. Now explain how you know using a sentence frame.
Re-check this step: ___. What place value / operation belongs here?
studentChoices: Choose how to show your thinking: equation, model, words, table, graph, or drawing.
Choose which problem you will explain to a partner.
Choose a challenge problem or a practice set to build fluency.
Choose your partner role: coach, recorder, checker, or explainer.
masteryChecklist: I can check if my answer makes sense.
I can solve a word problem.
reflectionCard: What student work is my evidence?
What will I adjust next time?

dataNextSteps.then: Assign or reteach the foundation resource (Get Ready / readiness).

dataNextSteps.if: Solved it but could not explain
dataNextSteps.then: Assign the sentence frame + partner explanation task.
Assign the extension, project, or challenge.
Assign the ESOL vocabulary + visual-model scaffold.
